Archival Description Title: Germany and Italy
Scope and Content: The files contain information on the relationship between Italy and Germany. They mention the axis between Rome and Berlin, a metaphor for the close ties between the two countries. Still, a distinction is made in the documents between Italian fascism and German Nazism. Mussolini and his politics are referenced and also portrayed in a negative light. Furthermore, the files discuss the Italian colonies such as Libya and criticize the annexation of South Tyrol, a region belonging to Austria. They analyze the Italian people and their traits and compare them to the Nordic race which is considered more moral and honorable.
Extent: 2 online resources (5, 183 pages)

Archival Description Title: Selected records from the Archivo Storico del Ministerio degli Affari Esteri
Scope and Content: This collection includes information on the Italian reaction to the rise of Nazi antisemitism in Germany and German-occupied territories, as well as on negotiations about the fate of Jews in southern France. The records also document the situation of refugees, the consequences of racial laws in Italy, the Italian resistance, and Zionism.
Extent: 6 microfilm reels, 16 mm

Archival Description Title: La résistance italienne
Scope and Content: The booklet written in French gives an overview of resistance movements in Italy during Fascism and later Nazi occupation. Acts of sabotage and armed struggle in various Italian locations are described, mainly from 1943 onwards. The structure of the partisan army is explained, the details of allied assistance are provided, and the difficulties encountered by the resistance are analyzed. During 1944 the fight became more organized, larger in scale and more successful. Casualties are listed and Italians fighting in the French army are given acknowledgment. The price of human life during these years is estimated at 33.000.
Extent: 1 electronic resource (27 pages)

Archival Description Title: Memorandum On The Situation in Italy
Scope and Content: The Italian Jewry can trace its origins back more than 2000 years until the 2nd century before Christ. Like no other Jewish community in Europe it has suffered less from persecution and disenfranchisement, due to the comparatively more tolerant but not necessarily benevolent attitude of native Italian rulers towards Jews in Italy. Persecutions or severe violent anti-Jewish outbreaks were usually induced by outside potentates and foreign powers. Discrimination held in Italy until the foundation of the unified Italian state in 1861, which granted Italian Jewry toleration. From toleration onward the Italian Jewry strived to make a positive contribution to Italian society in culture, politics, industry, economy and the sciences. Toleration also led to negative effects such as assimilation and numerous mixed marriages. Even the advent of fascism in Italy did not in the beginning diminish the Jews, as Italian fascism was not as anti-Semitic as German Nazism. Also Benito Mussolini did not share in the same anti-Semitic worldviews as Adolf Hitler. With the alignment of Fascist Italy and Nazism in Germany the Italian fascists have assimilated the anti-Semitic attitudes of Nazism, including the disenfranchisement of Italian Jewry according to the German model.
Extent: 1 electronic resource (14 pages)

Archival Description Title: Memorandum on the position of the Jews of Italy and Tripoli
Scope and Content: Due to the Axis Berlin-Rome the fascist regime allowed the unhindered defamation of Italian Jewry in the Italian media and public in accordance with the German demands of disenfranchisement and anti-Bolshevik propaganda. Despite the German demands to discriminate Jews and fight Bolshevism, various stakeholders in Italy influence the government's policies, such as the Catholic Church, the Monarchy, and the position of Italy as a Mediterranean power. The connections of the Church with the fascist regime are based on mutual interests such as anti-clericalism, anti-Bolshevism and others. The monarchy is positively motivated towards the Italian Jewry, since many Jews have helped it come to power and the royal family is therefore clearly philo-Semitic. The position of Italy as a Mediterranean power demands it to have a somewhat more pragmatic stance towards the Jews in the Mediterranean area than to its domestic Jewish population as the government finances rabbinical seminars in order to spread Rabbis across the Mediterranean with a positive attitude towards Italy. However, this Italian policy towards Mediterranean Jewry is contrasted by the demeanor of its officials in the North African colony of Tripolitania, which at some point heavily discriminate the Jewish population, in order to gain favor with the Arabs, on another mitigate those policies in order to maintain the support of Tripolitanian Jewry.
Extent: 1 electronic resource (7 pages)

Archival Description Title: The Jewish Problem in Italy
Scope and Content: The Jewish community of Italy is ancient and mostly fully assimilated into Italian society. High positions within the state and political parties have been occupied by Jewish citizens and demonstrate the degree of integration. The advent of fascism and the political alliance with national socialist Germany, lead to the complete disenfranchisement and discrimination of the Italian Jewry.
Extent: 1 electronic resource (6 pages)
